blocks.text: It is exactly the opposite of the synthesis. It involves the breaking down of the target molecule into less complicated, simpler and more readily available compounds which can serve as starting material. Retrosynthesis involves the disconnection approach.

blocks.alt: Target Molecule on the left and Starting Material on the right, joined by two open retrosynthetic arrows pointing to the starting material. A magenta loop labelled Retrosynthesis runs over the top from the target molecule down to the starting material; a cyan loop labelled Synthesis runs round the bottom from the starting material back up to the target molecule.
blocks.caption: Figure 25.1: Synthesis and retrosynthesis routes (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 25.1).

blocks.text: In retrosynthesis, those bonds of the target molecule are disconnected that result in a considerable structural simplification. Following a series of disconnections, we shall eventually arrive at simple, easily available starting materials.
